I’ve just edited the test script to filter out stale “end” messages for client B and also to drop any lingering “lobby” and “end” snapshots before closing client A’s socket. Those changes should address the two failing tests: the co‑op clear broadcast and the host migration when the original host leaves. 

Now I need to verify whether those modifications actually fix the failures. The most straightforward way is to run the multiplayer smoke test again, this time without the background server start/stop dance because the server is already running on the new port (4747) after I restarted it earlier. A simple synchronous execution of `node test-mp.mjs` with a reasonable timeout will give me the full test output and let me see if any of the previously failing assertions still fire.

Since the prior test run was invoked via a PowerShell command with a timeout, I’ll repeat that pattern: use the PowerShell tool, run `node test-mp.mjs`, give it a description, and set a timeout of 30 seconds (the same as before) to avoid hanging if something goes wrong. This will produce a fresh result I can inspect and decide the next steps.
